document.executive_summary: All four packages clear both client gates, so selection reduces to measured energy on the shared acceptance-batch basis. Verified order: P3 10 Wh, P2 22 Wh, P1 28 Wh, P4 49 Wh, with gaps +12, +18 and +39 Wh above the minimum. A's decision brief and B's verification memo agree on every decision-relevant number; B recomputed gates, ladder, spacing and ratios without arithmetic error, and both ballots were P3. I confirm the client-correct decision as P3. One quality issue is logged: A labelled P3's 4-of-5 defect position 'zero margin'; it actually leaves one defect of headroom, although A's regrade arithmetic (a two-defect regrade disqualifies P3, moving the win to P2) is correct. Figures were delivered empty under the no_figure delivery policy; source illustrations are archived. Cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability remain unverified. This handover passes the reconciliation, the error log and four open questions to the next analyst.
document.figure_caption: WO-03 handover view: A's brief and B's audit reconciled into one verified P3 decision, with the logged wording-slip issue and four open questions passed to the next analyst.

recommendation.rationale: Independently confirmed: all four packages pass both gates, and P3's 10 Wh measured energy is the lowest, 12 Wh below runner-up P2, on the identical acceptance-batch basis. A's and B's arithmetic match the trusted table throughout; the only logged defect is a 'zero margin' wording slip that changes no number. P3's 4/5 defect ceiling is a monitored contingency with P2 (22 Wh, zero defects) as fallback, not an override.

sections.body: A and B agree on all facts traced to the trusted table: eligibility (quality P4 98, P3 97, P2 95, P1 87; defects P1 0, P2 0, P4 2, P3 4), the energy ladder P3 10 Wh < P2 22 < P1 28 < P4 49, gaps +12/+18/+39 Wh, consecutive spacing 12/6/21 Wh, and cost ratios 2.2x and 4.9x versus the minimum. Both note that no tie-break applies and that quality differences are informational under the energy-first policy. The P3 decision follows from the policy alone; no disagreement exists between the two documents.
sections.heading: Reconciled verified findings

sections.body: Issue 1 (minor, logged): A called P3's 4-of-5 defect position 'zero margin' in two places; it actually leaves one defect of headroom. A's own regrade statement - two or more added defects disqualify P3 and move the win to P2 - is arithmetically correct, and B's audit confirmed the arithmetic but did not flag the wording. Issue 2 (delivery): the reserved figure boxes are empty in delivered copies under the no_figure policy; captions and the archived diagram remain usable. No other readability, truthfulness or usefulness defect was observed in either document.
sections.heading: Quality issues recorded

sections.body: Carried from A and B, unchanged: (1) is P3's 4-defect count stable - the single decision-relevant uncertainty, with P2 (22 Wh, zero defects) as fallback; (2) does the shared acceptance-batch basis persist across rounds, or should future work orders re-baseline; (3) will cost, delivery, maintenance or reliability evidence arrive - only the client can admit such factors; (4) what is the measurement uncertainty bound on the 10 Wh reading. All four are questions, not findings; none affects today's P3 selection.
sections.heading: Open questions carried forward

sections.body: Decisions this round: ballot P3 (client-correct, formed before reading B's memo), no joint finding and no sanction. Process notes for the next analyst: treat the trusted table as the only measurement source; recompute gates and the energy ladder before ranking; state facts and open questions separately; keep unverified cost, delivery and reliability claims out of the ranking; and monitor P3's defect margin as a contingency, not an override. The energy-first logic is expected to repeat unless the client changes the policy.
